title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation tool was used to create non-consensual intimate imagery of a real person. The person using the tool obtained source photos from the victim's private social media accounts and generated obscene deepfake images, then distributed them across multiple platforms under fake identities to conceal his involvement. The tool itself appears to have imposed no restrictions on the use case, either through technical safeguards or human review before generation.

This is a case of a system deployed without adequate control over who uses it and for what purpose. The failure occurred at the point of image generation, where no check existed to prevent creation of non-consensual sexual content. Catching it would have required either the AI system to refuse such requests, or human moderation of generated images before they could be shared.

It is not established whether the AI system was designed with safeguards that the user circumvented, or whether such safeguards were absent entirely.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and sharing explicit AI-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering from East Punjabi Bagh, obtained photos from the woman's private social media accounts and used artificial intelligence technology to generate obscene images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The victim, also 22 years old, discovered the abuse when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts alerting her to the morphed images and videos being circulated on Discord servers. She reported the crime to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. During their investigation, police analyzed digital footprints and traced connections between the fake profiles. When questioned, Bansal admitted he knew the victim from college and that personal conflict between them motivated his actions. Police recovered a mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence, with the investigation still ongoing.
